monument.purpose: The condensed table number in the margin column (aria-hidden); index numbers use the same width and weight at 2.25rem.

title.purpose: Table and notice titles at 88% width.

lead.purpose: The next-decision line, the masthead portal name, the titles of the add-a-document section and the withdraw panel, and governance section titles (bold, on a heavy rule).

body.purpose: Rows, totals and edition lines; tabular lining figures. Governance leads cap at 72ch, a search result's passage at 64ch; sub-index links in medium weight, bold when current.

label.purpose: Column heads (including governance tables), totals labels, field labels, the change notice heading, passage detail labels and the legend of a choices group, at 72% width, sentence case, ink 2.

meta.purpose: Notes, the masthead 'Valid as of' line, text buttons, Arabic secondary lines, the passage Where column, reasons and flags, the keys line, the save bar's state and reason lines, governance secondary lines, a search result's surrounding text, and sub-index links on phones. Key caps step down to 0.75rem.

arabic.purpose: Noto Sans Arabic for any lang=ar or dir=rtl content; a script fallback, not a design voice.

shadows.name: current-bar
shadows.purpose: A rule, not depth: the bar under the current index entry, the pressed filter and the current sub-index link. The only box-shadow in the system.

rules.name: rule-heavy
rules.purpose: Under the masthead, table heads, totals label, quiet line, notice head and change notice heading; above and below the processing line and the withdraw panel; at the foot of an open passage's detail row; on top of the save bar. Under a governance section title and a governance table's column heads.

rules.name: hairline
rules.purpose: Between rows, totals and governance table rows; 1px var(--rule) between tables, under the index and under a document's sub-index.

rules.name: double
rules.purpose: Above the notes at a table's foot.

motion.name: light
motion.purpose: Lighting a row, mark or note; background only, nothing reflows.

motion.name: extent
motion.purpose: Index extent rules settling to their share.

motion.name: busy-spin
motion.purpose: The refresh icon while tables reload.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All transitions and animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Priority-2 columns hide; margin column collapses; masthead unsticks; index stacks; sub-index tightens to 0.75rem gaps at meta size.

layout.name: save-bar-scroll-padding
layout.purpose: A passage moved to from the keyboard is never hidden under the sticky save bar.

layout.name: save-bar-stack
layout.value: z-index 4 (masthead 5); position static at 45rem and below
layout.purpose: The save bar stays in view on desktop, sits in flow on phones.

layout.name: governance-section
layout.value: padding-top 1rem; gap 0.75rem; lead max 72ch; form max 44rem; place column 14rem
layout.purpose: The rhythm of a document's governance pages.

layout.name: search-bar
layout.value: field flex 1 1 28rem; field and action at min-height 2.25rem; align-items end; wraps
layout.purpose: One field and its action at one height; the button wraps beneath on phones.

narrative.overview:
The portal is set like a national railway timetable book. Each area of shared knowledge is a numbered table. Its number stands monumental and condensed in a left margin column. The table beside it has an exact column set, and each sourced fact carries a reference mark that leads to a numbered note at the table's foot. The page is near-white neutral stock with black ink. Hierarchy comes from three rule weights and from type weight, never from containers, fills or colour. Two colours are held back, and each has exactly one job.

The density is that of a reference work. Rows are tight (0.5rem block padding) and separated by hairlines. Numbers and dates use tabular, lining figures and sit right-aligned, as in any timetable. The surface is flat: no cards, no shadows for depth, no pills, no gradients. One sticky masthead strip and an index of the tables bind the book, and every screen sits inside that binding.

The interface language is English. It calls the indexed units of a document "passages", and the units of the table-aware cut "fields"; it never says "chunks". Content keeps its own language and direction. Arabic names render in Noto Sans Arabic, in their own direction, beside the English in the same cell. The theme is light only. This is a decision for an office-daylight scene, not an omission.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white neutral stock (never cream) and black ink; flat, ruled, unboxed.
One grotesk (Archivo Variable) in several widths: 100% for text, 88% for titles, 72% for labels, 62% for monumental table numbers.
Weight shows rank. Colour has only two jobs: red for disruption, blue for reference.
Three rule weights: a 2px heavy rule, a 1px hairline and a 3px double rule.
Notes are numbered in reading order. A mark and its note light each other.
Rows never reflow when a state changes. Only the background changes.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Colour has exactly two jobs. Red marks a disruption. Blue marks a reference, meaning something you can follow, plus focus. No other hue appears, and neither colour ever decorates or ranks.

rules.name: The Stock Not Cream Rule
rules.body: The page is neutral near-white (`stock`). Never warm it toward paper or cream.

rules.name: The Weight Is Rank Rule
rules.body: A row's importance is set by weight and ink, never by colour or badge. A due row has its name and status in bold (680). A delayed row has its status in bold and in disruption red. A running row is set in ink 2, a row in service in regular ink, a past row in ink 3.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Contrast comes from Archivo's width and weight axes, not from a second display face. Noto Sans Arabic is a script fallback, not a design voice.

rules.name: The Three Rules Rule
rules.body: Separation uses three weights only. A 2px heavy rule sits under the masthead and every table head, totals label, notice head and governance section title. A 1px hairline sits between rows, totals and tables. A 3px double rule sits above the notes. Do not add a fourth weight or a box.

rules.name: The Edit Mark Exception
rules.body: The edit mark is the one scoped exception to the reference-mark grammar: a letter, not a number, and it opens its passage in place instead of leading to a numbered note. A review holds thousands of passages, and numbered notes for every edit would bury the table's foot. Use it only for an edit to a passage; every sourced fact still takes a numbered mark and note.

rules.name: The Kept Column Rule
rules.body: In a governance table, a secondary fact (a version's cut and passage count, a handover's reason or who performed it, a citation's place or version, a field's label) rides as a secondary ink-2 meta line inside a kept column, never in a column of its own. Columns still drop by priority on phones, and these facts stay with the row.

rules.name: The Passages Rule
rules.body: On screen the indexed units of a document are "passages", and the units of the table-aware cut are "fields". The cut itself reads "Passages" or "Table-aware". The word "chunk" belongs to code, never to a label, heading, count or caption.

dos: Do put every area in a numbered table: a monumental number in the 7.5rem margin column, a title, an edition line, a ruled grid, notes and one next-decision line.
Do show a row's rank by weight and ink: bold for due, red and bold status for delayed, ink 2 for running, ink 3 for past.
Do give every sourced fact a reference mark, and number the notes in reading order.
Do keep lit states to a background wash (`reference-wash`), so rows and cells never reflow or change size.
Do open a focused passage in place on the stock band (`stock-band`), with its detail row closing on a heavy rule.
Do keep deliberate steps such as withdrawal inline and ruled under the head.
Do say why a disabled action waits, in a line linked to it.
Do put a governance table's secondary facts on a secondary ink-2 meta line in a kept column, so phones keep them when columns drop.
Do mark the current page of a document's sub-index in bold ink with the inset 3px ink bar, and show the unsaved count on Review.
Do say "passages" for indexed units and "fields" for the table-aware cut.
Do use tabular, lining figures, and end-align numbers and dates.
Do let content keep its own direction: `dir="auto"` on names, `lang="ar" dir="rtl"` on Arabic secondary lines, set in Noto Sans Arabic.
Do keep targets at least 24px (text buttons 1.5rem, return links 1.5rem) and show the 2px blue focus outline on everything focusable.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`. All transitions and animations collapse to 0.01ms.
donts: Don't use colour for anything except disruption (red) and reference or focus (blue).
Don't add cards, panels, elevation shadows, pills, badges or gradients. Separation comes from the three rule weights.
Don't warm the stock toward cream or paper.
Don't add a second display typeface. Width and weight on Archivo carry the contrast.
Don't add a dark theme without a new decision. Light only is the chosen office-daylight scene.
Don't scroll tables sideways. Drop columns by priority instead.
Don't open a modal or a card to edit or withdraw. Rows open in place; steps open inline.
Don't extend the letter edit mark beyond edited passages. Sourced facts keep numbered marks and notes.
Don't give a secondary fact (a cut, a count, a reason, a place) its own column.
